subject: forensic-medicine
title: Mercury Poisoning, Acrodynia and Copper Poisoning

steps.title: Mercury forms and corrosive sublimate
steps.tx: **Mercury or quicksilver** is a bright silvery liquid metal, volatile at room temperature. Mercuric compounds are soluble and intensely poisonous; mercurous compounds are far less soluble and less active. Swallowed metallic mercury is not absorbed and is not poisonous, while inhaled vapour and finely divided metal on skin or mucosa are absorbed. Mercuric chloride, corrosive sublimate, is the classic poison: colourless prismatic crystals with a styptic metallic taste, fatal at one to two grams in three to five days.
steps.say: Swallowed quicksilver passes harmlessly, but its vapour and soluble mercuric salts kill at one to two grams.

steps.title: Two phases of acute mercury poisoning
steps.tx: Acute mercuric poisoning runs in **two phases**. First come acrid metallic taste, throat constriction, hoarse voice, corroded greyish white mouth and fauces, burning pain, vomiting of greyish bloody mucoid material with membrane shreds, bloody diarrhoea with tenesmus and early circulatory collapse. In one to three days the second phase brings glossitis and ulcerative gingivitis with loosening teeth and jaw necrosis, then tubular necrosis with polyuria, albuminuria, uraemia and acidosis, and later membranous colitis with dysentery.
steps.say: First the corroded mouth and bloody gut, then in days the ulcerated gums and necrosed kidneys define mercuric poisoning.

steps.title: Chronic mercury: tremor, gums and erethism
steps.tx: **Chronic mercury poisoning or hydrargyrism** shows a classic triad of gingivitis with salivation, tremors and neuropsychiatric change. Salivation, sore mouth, a blue gum line, loosening teeth and progressive uraemia accompany moderately coarse tremor beginning in the hands and spreading to lips, tongue, arms and legs: Danbury tremors, hatter's shakes, worst as concussio mercurialis where no activity is possible. Mercurial erethism adds anxiety, shyness, irritability, memory loss and suicidal melancholia, the mad hatter picture.
steps.say: Salivating gums, hatter's tremor and shy irritable erethism are chronic mercury's triad in workers and mirror makers.

steps.tx: **Chronic mercury poisoning or hydrargyrism** shows gingivitis with salivation, tremor, and mental change. Sore mouth, a blue gum line, loose teeth, and progressive uraemia travel with it. Moderately coarse tremor begins in the hands, the hatter shakes or Danbury tremors, then reaches lips, tongue, arms, and legs. In concussio mercurialis no useful movement remains. Mercurial erethism adds anxiety, shyness, irritability, failing memory, and suicidal melancholia. Handwriting that collapses down the page is the hand tremor made visible.
steps.say: Chronic mercury brings salivating sore gums, a tremor that starts in the hands and spreads, and a shy irritable erethism that can reach suicidal melancholia. When the shakes are worst, coordinated movement stops, and handwriting falls apart.

vis.alt: A handwriting sample deteriorates line by line during examination for hatter tremor.
vis.caption: Script grows coarser and less controlled down the page, matching the tremor of chronic mercury poisoning. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Mercurialentis and acrodynia
steps.tx: Two named curiosities complete mercury. **Mercurialentis** is a brownish deposit of mercury on the anterior lens capsule seen by slit lamp as a malt brown reflex, bilateral and harmless to vision. **Acrodynia or pink disease** is an idiosyncratic hypersensitivity of children to chronic mercury in any form: insidious anorexia, insomnia, sweating, itchy generalised rash and photophobia, with hands and feet puffy, painful and paraesthetic with peeling skin, sometimes shedding teeth. Minamata disease is the organic mercury disaster from contaminated fish in Japan in 1956.
steps.say: A brown lens reflex that spares vision and a pink peeling rash in children are mercury's two named signatures.

rows: Malt brown lens reflex, vision kept

steps.title: Treating mercury without making it worse
steps.tx: **Mercury treatment** binds first: milk, egg white, salt poor albumin, sodium formaldehyde sulphoxylate or sodium bicarbonate lavage, cathartics withheld, whole bowel irrigation considered. BAL is the chelating agent of choice on the arsenic regimen; penicillamine serves less severe vapour and inorganic poisoning, two hundred fifty milligrams four times daily for five days in adults. Two traps are examined: BAL with penicillamine together can form a toxic compound, and calcium EDTA must not be used because it is nephrotoxic with mercury. Haemodialysis answers significant kidney damage.
steps.say: BAL for mercury, penicillamine for milder cases, never BAL with penicillamine together, and never EDTA near mercury kidneys.

nodes.label: Bind with milk or egg white

steps.title: Copper sulphate, blue vitriol
steps.tx: **Copper** metal itself is not poisonous, but its compounds powerfully inhibit enzymes. Copper sulphate, blue vitriol, forms large blue crystals; copper subacetate or verdigris is bluish green. Symptoms begin in fifteen to thirty minutes with metallic taste, salivation, burning and colicky pain, thirst and repeated vomiting of blue or green material, then liquid brown non bloody diarrhoea with straining. Copper sulphate kills at thirty grams and subacetate at fifteen, in one to three days.
steps.say: Blue green vomit within half an hour of blue crystals is copper sulphate until the stomach contents prove otherwise.

steps.tx: Metallic copper is not itself poisonous, but its compounds powerfully inhibit enzymes. **Copper sulphate**, called blue vitriol, forms large blue crystals, while subacetate or verdigris is bluish green. Symptoms start in fifteen to thirty minutes with metallic taste, salivation, burning colicky pain, thirst, and repeated blue or green vomit, followed by liquid brown diarrhoea without blood and with straining. Sulphate kills at about thirty grams and subacetate at fifteen, usually within one to three days.
steps.say: Blue vitriol crystals cause metallic taste, colic, and blue or green vomit within half an hour, then straining brown diarrhoea. About thirty grams of copper sulphate, or fifteen of verdigris, can kill in one to three days.

vis.alt: Blue green vomit in a kidney tray sits beside crystals of blue vitriol.
vis.caption: Brightly coloured gastric contents match the blue crystals of copper sulphate collected at the scene. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Copper treatment and postmortem colours
steps.tx: **Copper poisoning treatment** washes the stomach with one percent potassium ferrocyanide, forming insoluble cupric ferrocyanide, forbids emetics, gives demulcents that form insoluble copper albuminate, castor oil to clear the bowel, early haemodialysis and chelation with penicillamine, EDTA or BAL. At autopsy the skin may be yellow, greenish blue froth sits at mouth and nostrils, and gastric mucosa and contents are greenish or bluish over a soft fatty liver with proximal tubular degeneration.
steps.say: Ferrocyanide in the wash and penicillamine after it treat copper, whose green blue stomach signs its name postmortem.

steps.title: Chalcosis and Wilson disease confusion
steps.tx: Copper deposited in tissues is **chalcosis**: a pigmented ring in the deeper cornea, green hair from copper algicides in swimming pools, a green line on the gums in chronic poisoning, vineyard sprayer's granulomatous lung from inhaled copper sulphate spray, and peripheral neuritis with muscle atrophy. Reddy notes chronic poisoning causes Wilson's disease in his framing; the examiner's practical point is that tissue copper overload, occupational or metabolic, converges on cornea, liver, lung and nerve.
steps.say: Green hair, a corneal ring and sprayer's lung are chalcosis, copper written into cornea, hair and lung by chronic exposure.

steps.title: Circumstances of copper and mercury cases
steps.tx: Both metals poison mostly by accident in **copper and mercury circumstances**. Copper's colour and taste forbid homicide and make suicide rare; food cooked in untinned copper vessels and greened with verdigris, children swallowing attractive blue crystals, abortifacient use and cattle poisoning fill the casebook. Mercury accidents come from strong solutions used to wash abscess cavities or irrigate vagina, uterus or rectum, and from contraceptive or abortifacient vaginal introduction; homicidal and suicidal mercury is rare.
steps.say: Untinned vessels, blue crystals and irrigation accidents poison with copper and mercury far oftener than any murderer does.
